top_signal.title: Selling or stepping back from an established £85k turnover web design business – what would you do?
top_signal.summary: I'm looking for some advice from people who have sold small service businesses, or successfully stepped back from running one.   I've been running my own web and graphic design business since around 2010, operating as a limited company since 2018 (my spouse and I are both directors).   The business is profitable, established and has a loyal client base, but it's essentially a one-person operation. I do all the work myself, although I have a few trusted freelancers I can call on when things get busy.   I'm now at a stage where I'd like to significantly reduce my involvement, or potentially exit altogether. I'm not in any particular rush, so I have some flexibility in how I approach this.   **Financial overview:**   * **Annual turnover:** Approximately £85k, fairly steady year-on-year. Previously VAT registered for a couple of years when a larger client increased their workload, but deregistered last year.  * **£15k/year:** Website hosting and maintenance plans. Largely passive recurring income.  * **£20k/year:** Small website updates, support and maintenance work for existing hosting clients. Generally straightforward work.  * **£15k/year:** Running virtual events for one long-standing client.  * **£30k/year:** Designing and building new websites. This is the most time-consuming and demanding part of the business.  * **Gross profit:** Approximately £81–82k, reflecting very low overheads, with a good proportion of the income comes from long-standing client relationships rather
